summary.tldr: Changes insolvency rules so some unpaid pension, group insurance and severance claims get priority in bankruptcy and creditor proceedings.
what_it_does: Adds unpaid special pension payments and other unfunded pension liabilities or solvency deficiencies to the priority list in bankruptcy.
Adds the same pension-related claims to creditor proceedings under the Companies’ Creditors Arrangement Act.
Gives priority in bankruptcy to amounts needed to protect beneficiaries if an employer stops taking part in a group insurance plan, including life, disability, health or dental coverage.
Adds unpaid severance pay or pay in lieu of notice, after any amount already paid by the trustee, to the bankruptcy priority list.
Requires creditor-protection proceedings to give amounts at least equal to the bankruptcy priority amounts for group insurance and severance claims.
Delays some new rules for existing employers and companies in prescribed pension plans until the third anniversary of royal assent.
who_it_affects: People covered by group insurance plans
summary.background: It amends the Bankruptcy and Insolvency Act and the Companies’ Creditors Arrangement Act.
